queryLatencyEndToEnd_10queries_x5reps.honestComparison: Native's full lexical pipeline is now SLOWER end-to-end than WebView's, median 2114.6ms vs 707.6ms (native ~3x slower), a reversal from the stage-1 'simplified matcher' comparison (325.5ms vs 1481ms, native ~4.5x faster) where native only ran one FTS5 query per search. The full port carries real per-query cost this spike had not paid before: RapidFuzz alias/medication-spelling fuzzy matching over the whole alias vocabulary, multiple SQL branch executions with bm25 + hydration each, and Kotlin-side fusion/grouping/ranking - none of that existed in the stage-1 matcher. This is not a JIT/interpreter artifact of one slow run: the pipelineInternalMedianMs of 1964.6ms tracks the end-to-end number closely across all 50 samples (see raw data), so the cost is inside runLookupPipelineGroups itself, not framework overhead around it. No attempt was made to optimize the port's hot path (e.g. RapidFuzz over all aliases per query with no early-exit/pre-filter) - that would be legitimate follow-up work if this port is to be kept, not a claim made here.

scrolling_5runs_20swipes_strict8_33msBud.jankBasis: strict >8.33ms (120Hz budget), per the coordinator's explicit instruction this stage - unlike the prior pass's Android-own-threshold numbers, both apps are ~100% 'janky' under this stricter budget at every run; native's p50 is modestly better (21.8ms vs 27.4ms, native ~1.26x faster) but the gap is far smaller than the stage-1 pass suggested

memoryAfterQueryPlusScrollSession.note: Native's full-pipeline PSS (~133 MB) is now HIGHER than WebView's (~118 MB), a reversal from the stage-1 comparison (70359 vs 114349 KB, native ~1.6x smaller). The QueryDocumentIndex (built from all ~20k documents) plus the full alias vocabulary held in memory for the process lifetime is the likely cause; not root-caused further within this pass's time budget - flagged as a real cost of the full port, not glossed over. Two earlier same-session readings (140400 KB pre-scroll-fix-retry, 124684 KB from a stale/backgrounded process) are consistent with this being in the 120-140 MB band, not a one-off spike.

apkSize.note: Native's APK is still ~6.7x smaller than WebView's (unchanged conclusion from stage 1 - the full pipeline port added Kotlin/JVM code, not new native dependencies)

methodologyNotes: Re-discovered and re-fixed the same multi-word-Cyrillic adb broadcast re-split bug documented in postFixMeasurements.methodologyBugsFixed while capturing an ad hoc post-session PSS reading (manually invoking `adb shell am broadcast ... --es query "<text with spaces>"` as separate shell argv elements instead of one pre-quoted string) - a reminder that this bug is specific to how the invocation is built each time, not something fixed once in a script and permanently safe from a differently-written one-off command.

The native app being merely process-alive but backgrounded (screen showing a different foreground app) silently prevented its Compose LaunchedEffect/withFrameNanos callbacks from ever firing, so a broadcast sent while backgrounded appeared to succeed (result=0) but produced no bench log at all until the app was brought back to the foreground - worth knowing for anyone re-running these scripts unattended.

optimizationPass.description: One optimization pass with a stopping criterion, per user decision: if native query latency is not faster than WebView by median AND PSS is not lower, freeze the port and keep WebView.

profiling_10queries_x5reps_meanStageMs.note: Measured AFTER the alias/medication-spelling index rebuild-per-query bug was fixed. Before that fix, aliases+spelling dominated everything else combined (index rebuild over the whole 44,214-row alias table every query). ranking is now the largest single cost, followed by fusion - neither was suspected before this pass.

optimizationsApplied: Cache createAliasExpander/createMedicationSpellingMatcher once in LookupEngine instead of rebuilding from the whole ~44,214-row alias table on every query (the dominant pre-fix cost) - LookupPipeline.kt/MedicationLookupPlan.kt already accepted these as optional params (for golden-parity tests), LookupEngine just wasn't passing its own vocabulary through them

Verified against create-medical-core.ts (~line 1184): queryDocumentIndex and TS's own alias/medication-spelling WeakMap caches are built LAZILY on the first search() call, not at WebView startup - corrected 3 stale comments in the Kotlin port that claimed otherwise
Moved vocabulary + QueryDocumentIndex construction to a background coroutine kicked off right after LookupEngine construction, not blocking first frame or the first query

Found and fixed a real native SIGSEGV crash this background warm-up introduced: two concurrent coroutines both touching NativeSearchDatabase's single non-thread-safe SQLiteConnection at once (bundled SQLite JNI bridge). Fixed by serializing both builds onto one coroutine.

Removed QueryDocumentIndex's dead byId: Map<String, SearchDocumentSummary> (a full second copy of all ~20k documents, confirmed unused outside its own definition), computing availableIds directly instead

Added manual string-pooling (not kotlin.text.intern(), which is JVM-only) for low-cardinality DB columns retained for the process lifetime: category/canonicalTerm in listAliases(), sourceType in listSearchDocuments()

Considered, not pursued: primitive IntArray-keyed alternatives to Aliases.kt/MedicationSpelling.kt's small (~1-30 distinct keys) token-length HashMaps - negligible boxing overhead next to the ~20k-document/~44k-alias structures

environmentalCaveat.response: Every number below was re-measured for BOTH apps back-to-back in the SAME current (degraded) session, for an environment-invariant relative comparison, rather than comparing fresh native numbers against stale (cleaner-environment) WebView numbers from stage 4. Absolute values here are inflated vs. stage 4's and should not be read as steady-state performance. Full host-level fix (freeing disk space) was out of scope for this agent to perform unilaterally.

queryLatencyEndToEnd_10queries_x5reps.comparison: Native ~1.68x faster at median, ~3.7x faster at p95 - a reversal from stage 4's own pass (native 2114.6ms vs webview 707.6ms, native ~3x SLOWER then).

scrolling_5runs_20swipes_strict8_33msBud.comparison: Native ahead at every percentile, ~1.36x faster median.

memoryAfterQueryPlusScrollSession.note: PSS did not improve relative to WebView (native still ~1.3x higher, essentially unchanged from stage 4's 136567 vs 120836 KB). The byId removal and string-pooling fixes measurably shrink retained memory but not enough to close this gap; QueryDocumentIndex's four identity maps and the full AliasRecord list held for the process lifetime remain the likely largest contributors, not root-caused further this pass.

native.note: vocabularyBuildMs (20-24s for a CPU-bound sort/tokenize over 44,214 alias rows) is almost certainly inflated by the environmental degradation described above, not by this pass's own logic - NOT re-verified in a clean environment before this report, stated as measured and flagged as suspect.

webview.note: single sample this pass (vs stage 4's 5-run 700-853ms range) - also degraded vs stage 4, confirming the slowdown is environment-wide, not native-specific

stoppingCriterionDecision.criterion: if native query is not faster than WebView by median AND PSS is not lower, honestly write 'keep WebView, port frozen'
stoppingCriterionDecision.decision: CONTINUE the port; do not freeze
stoppingCriterionDecision.reasoning: The freeze condition's first half (native not faster) is false, so the conjunction is false regardless of PSS - the criterion as stated does not trigger a freeze.
honestCaveats: PSS is still higher for native, not lower - a real, disclosed tradeoff, not hidden by the 'continue' decision
Absolute numbers were measured on a degraded host (98% disk full, ~85MB free RAM) and should be re-verified on a clean host before being treated as a stable baseline
ranking (51.1% of pipeline time) and fusion (19.9%) are now the dominant remaining per-query costs and were not touched this pass
vocabularyBuildMs needs its own clean-environment re-measurement before being trusted as a real cold-start number
